title: Cross-Disease Mapping of Immune Polarization and Metabolic Demand
content: Immune activation requires coordinated changes in both adaptive immune-cell programs and cellular metabolism, yet it remains unclear whether these dimensions follow shared patterns across diseases. We analyzed publicly available whole-blood transcriptomic data from seven independent cohorts spanning six conditions (autism spectrum disorder on two platforms, sepsis, Crohn’s disease, allergic disease, pediatric systemic lupus erythematosus, and dementia/cognitiveimpairment). Adaptive immune polarization architecture (AIPA) was defined from six CD4-associated transcriptional programs (TH1, TH2, TH17, Tfh, FOXP3-Treg, and Tr1-like). Metabolic demand was quantified with the τ-axis (TAO); gap metrics measured the match between demand and the corresponding transcriptional metabolic response.TH1 and Tr1-like formed the most conserved component of AIPA across all seven cohorts, whereas TH2, TH17, Tfh, and FOXP3-Treg showed greater disease-dependent variation. Similar CD4-associated immune states were accompanied by markedly different levels of metabolic demand and different capacities to meet that demand. Despite these disease-specific differences, one pattern was consistent: TCA/OXPHOS induction was higher inTH1/Tr1/Tfh/Treg-dominant than in TH2/TH17-dominant disease samples in every cohort. These findings extend a previously developed demand–execution framework and demonstrate that immune configuration and metabolic response are complementary but distinct dimensions of disease state. They further identify a reproducible mitochondrial-oxidative transcriptional signature linked to CD4-pole organization across diverse diseases.
